skill.name: workflow-automation
skill.description: Create repeatable development workflows for builds, tests, setup, deployments, Git hooks, and CI. Covers npm scripts, Makefiles, shell scripts, Husky, lint-staged, Docker, and GitHub Actions.
skill.summary: Generate npm scripts, Make targets, Git hooks, shell scripts, and CI workflows for repeatable development automation.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives for Markdown code fences, documentation links, /dev/null redirects, and guarded .env template creation. No prompt injection attempt was found. Semantic review identified operational risks from destructive cleanup examples, SSH deployment commands, and non-immutable third-party CI action pinning.

remediation.suggestion: Limit cleanup targets to generated artifacts and require explicit confirmation before deleting dependency or user-controlled directories.

remediation.issue: Deployment examples run SSH commands against staging and production hosts.
remediation.suggestion: Add dry-run support, host allowlists, and explicit user confirmation before remote deployment commands are generated or run.

remediation.issue: The CI example uses a third-party action by mutable version tag.
remediation.suggestion: Pin third-party GitHub Actions to immutable commit SHAs or explain the trust decision in the generated workflow.

remediation.issue: Generated automation can install packages, start services, and change project state.
remediation.suggestion: State that users should review generated commands before execution and keep automation scoped to the current project.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Cleanup Commands Included
semantic_findings.description: The skill shows cleanup tasks that remove directories with rm -rf, while later saying destructive commands should not run without confirmation. Generated workflows should require explicit approval before deleting files.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The removal commands and the safety rule are both present in SKILL.md. The commands target project-local paths, so the likely impact is moderate.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Deployment Commands Target Production Hosts
semantic_findings.description: The deployment example runs SSH commands against staging and production host aliases and restarts services. Copied without review, generated scripts could modify live systems.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The SSH deployment commands are explicit in the script example. The risk depends on user configuration, but the live-system impact is clear.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party CI Action Is Not Pinned Immutably
semantic_findings.description: The GitHub Actions example uses a third-party Codecov action by version tag rather than an immutable commit. This can increase supply chain risk in generated CI workflows.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The third-party action reference is visible in the workflow example. Tag pinning is common but weaker than commit pinning for supply chain control.

content.value_statement: Teams lose time repeating setup, build, test, and deployment commands. This skill creates practical workflow templates for npm, Make, hooks, scripts, and CI.
actual_capabilities: Drafts npm script sets for development, builds, tests, linting, formatting, Docker, and cleanup tasks.
Creates Makefile targets that wrap common project commands behind a consistent interface.
Defines Husky and lint-staged checks for pre-commit quality gates.
Builds shell script templates for development setup and deployment workflows.
Creates GitHub Actions CI workflows for lint, type check, test, build, and coverage upload.
Shows a project automation file layout for scripts, Makefiles, package configuration, and Git hooks.
limitations: Examples require adaptation before use in real projects.
Generated commands can change files or remote systems if run without review.
The skill assumes common Node.js, npm, Docker, Make, Husky, and GitHub Actions workflows.
Deployment examples use placeholder hosts and paths that must be replaced safely.

use_cases.title: Standardize Local Commands
use_cases.description: Create npm scripts and Make targets so every developer runs the same build, test, lint, and setup commands.

use_cases.title: Prepare Project Onboarding
use_cases.description: Generate setup scripts and documented automation so new contributors can prepare a development environment faster.

use_cases.title: Create CI Baselines
use_cases.description: Draft GitHub Actions workflows that run validation checks for pull requests and main branch changes.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Scripts
prompt_templates.prompt: Create npm scripts for a Node.js project with development, build, test, lint, format, and type check commands.

prompt_templates.title: Add Make Targets
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Makefile that wraps my npm scripts and includes help, install, dev, build, test, lint, clean, and ci targets.

prompt_templates.title: Automate Quality Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up Husky and lint-staged for a TypeScript project. Include checks for formatting, linting, type checking, and changed tests.

prompt_templates.title: Design Full Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a complete workflow automation plan with setup scripts, safe cleanup, Docker commands, GitHub Actions CI, and reviewed deployment steps.

output_examples.input: Create workflow automation for a new TypeScript service.
output_examples.output: A structured plan with npm tasks, Make targets, pre-commit checks, setup steps, and CI validation stages.

output_examples.input: Help our team standardize pull request checks.
output_examples.output: A workflow outline covering linting, formatting, type checks, tests, coverage upload, and branch-based CI triggers.

output_examples.input: Prepare deployment automation for staging and production.
output_examples.output: A deployment script design with build, test, environment selection, remote command review, and confirmation safeguards.

best_practices: Review every generated command before running it locally or in CI.
Keep automation idempotent, project-scoped, and documented for team use.
Use confirmation prompts or dry-run modes for cleanup and deployment tasks.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated cleanup or deployment commands without checking their targets.
Do not hardcode secrets, tokens, passwords, or private host details in scripts.
Do not copy placeholder paths, service names, or hosts into production unchanged.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It generates workflow templates for npm scripts, Makefiles, Git hooks, shell scripts, Docker tasks, and GitHub Actions.

faq.question: Can it run the automation for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides templates and guidance. Users should review commands before running them.

faq.question: Is it only for Node.js projects?
faq.answer: Most examples target Node.js workflows, but the Makefile and script patterns can be adapted to other stacks.

faq.question: Does it include deployment workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes deployment script patterns, but real deployment commands need careful review and project-specific safeguards.

faq.question: Can it create GitHub Actions workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft CI workflows for linting, type checks, tests, builds, and coverage upload.

faq.question: How should teams use it safely?
faq.answer: Treat generated scripts as drafts, validate paths and hosts, remove secrets, and require confirmation for destructive actions.
